solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A page on average about Mudd's employers that's insincere

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, here the average wrapping the newspaper

parts.note: so-so means middling, about average
Mudd is the setter, who works for the Financial Times, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: A newspaper page praising the setter's own employers sounds like flattery nobody means.
explanation.walkthrough: Soft soap is usually a noun or verb for flattery; here it is used as an adjective for words meant only to please.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is flattering talk not sincerely meant, so used attributively it describes something hollow and false.

clue.text: Drug with oxygen, one's affected by applying the gas

definitions.text: one's affected by applying the gas

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A drug mixed with oxygen affects anyone who breathes in the gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' is the accelerator pedal: pressing it raises the reading on the speedometer, informally a speedo.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedo is short for speedometer, whose needle rises when the driver presses the accelerator.

clue.text: Insect eating grass that's light

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the insect wraps round the grass

parts.note: a fly is an insect
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: An insect munching grass seems weightless.
explanation.definitionFit: Floaty describes something light and airy, such as a flowing fabric.

clue.text: Emaciated local passing through the heavens

indicators.note: passing through means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
a local is a British pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A gaunt neighbour drifts across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, which is what emaciated describes in its extreme form.

clue.text: At which point discarded letters left, so thrown back into rubbish heap

indicators.note: into places the turned pair inside the rearranged letters
rubbish signals that heap is jumbled
thrown back means the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Letters thrown away are put back into a rubbish heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown back' turns PORTSO into OSTROP, which goes into APHE, 'rubbish' rearranging HEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe marks where letters have been omitted, as in can't for cannot.

clue.text: Coup rests on companion

parts.note: to rest something somewhere is to put it there, so rests gives puts
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A coup's success depends on loyal allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places one piece after the other, as in a down clue resting on another.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a coup by another name.

clue.text: Purist as debauched on another level

indicators.note: debauched means corrupted, so the letters are perverted into a new order

explanation.surface: A purist turned debauched has reached another plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstairs means on a higher floor of a building, another level up.

clue.text: Main work, while in steps to appear ascendant, prose ultimately

indicators.note: in places the conjunction inside the reversed steps
in a down clue, ascendant means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: paces are steps
as can mean while

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of prose

explanation.surface: An artist's chief work climbs steps while prose comes last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear ascendant' reverses the steps, since a down answer reads upwards; 'ultimately' takes E from prose. 'Main' is the sea, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture of the sea, and the main is a poetic word for the sea.

clue.text: Horticulturalist's building, wetter around you

indicators.note: around means the watering device encloses the pronoun

parts.note: a hose wets things, so it is a wetter
thou is the old word for you

explanation.surface: A gardener's building has a wetter around for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is a heated greenhouse where gardeners grow tender plants.

clue.text: After retraction of single volume, Tory smiley, perhaps?

indicators.note: after places the Tory piece at the end
retraction is drawing back, so the single volume is read backwards

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is single
a tome is a large book or volume
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician grins once a single book has been withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face is one example of an emoticon, a small face made from keyboard characters; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Point within atlas worryingly sloping

indicators.note: within puts the compass point inside the rearranged letters
worryingly suggests the letters of atlas are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A map in an atlas tilts alarmingly off its true angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worryingly' rearranges ATLAS into ASLAT, and N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slant, tilted diagonally away from upright.

clue.text: Greek character famous for retreating, set off

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the pair is read in reverse

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
noted means well known, famous

explanation.surface: A famous Greek figure in retreat sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses both pieces as one run; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to trigger its explosion, which is to make it go bang.

clue.text: Not entirely inelegant, old cowboy

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: gauche means awkward, lacking grace

explanation.surface: An old cowboy is not entirely without grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter of the synonym for inelegant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a horseman of the South American pampas, the local equivalent of a cowboy.

clue.text: Annex state amid flagrant violation?

indicators.note: amid places the state abbreviation in the middle of the rearranged letters
a violation breaks something, so the letters of flagrant are broken up

parts.note: NY is New York, a US state

explanation.surface: A dispute over a granny annex becomes a blatant breach of state planning law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violation' rearranges the letters of flagrant before the state goes in. A granny flat is a British term for a self-contained annex for an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny flat is an annex built onto or beside a house for a relative, so annex is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Acidic fruit with a bitter aftertaste?

definitions.meaning: literally, grapes that taste tart and unripe
figuratively, the resentment of someone who disparages what they failed to get

explanation.definitionFit: Literally tart grapes, and idiomatically the pretence that something unattained was never wanted, from Aesop's fox.

clue.text: A chest's covered, bandaging one graze

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping round, so the covered phrase encloses one

parts.note: read as bra's on, the chest is covered
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chest is covered, with a bandage on one graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest's covered' is read as the phrase 'bra's on', BRASON, which wraps I.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a scrape of the skin, which is what a graze is.

clue.text: Train to masticate repeatedly, say

indicators.note: repeatedly here means the chewing word is given twice over
say signals that the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to masticate is to chew

explanation.surface: A trainee is told to chew food again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Choo-choo is childish talk for a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Choo-choo is a nursery word for a steam train, from the sound it makes.

clue.text: Trouble for Asian holidaying in Africa?

indicators.note: trouble means disturbance, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller runs into trouble on holiday in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on safari means on a trip to see wildlife, typically in Africa; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: From which one might snigger when late?

definitions.meaning: one sniggers from behind a hand raised to hide the laugh

explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means behind schedule or in arrears; read as two words it is where one hides a snigger.

clue.text: Not hard in poor harvest — to do this?

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not hard means the letter for hard is removed from the word

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: With a poor harvest, people may go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' drops H from HARVEST, and 'poor' rearranges ARVEST. The definition looks back at the poor harvest: what people do after one.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from lack of food, the likely result of a failed harvest.

clue.text: Accent afoot?

definitions.meaning: worn on the foot, a sturdy shoe

explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is both a strong Irish or Scottish accent and a stout leather shoe with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Drawer in chalet's apparently turned upside down

indicators.note: turned upside down says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drawer in a chalet has apparently been turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is not furniture but something to draw with. In a down clue 'turned upside down' reads LETSAP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a chalky crayon used for drawing, so it is a drawer in the sense of a tool that draws.

clue.text: A letter read out as an acknowledgement

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a vowel is one kind of letter

explanation.surface: Reading a letter aloud amounts to an admission.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or admission, an acknowledgement of something.

clue.text: Panic this year after meltdown

indicators.note: a meltdown is a collapse, so the letters of this year fall apart and reform

explanation.surface: A year of financial meltdown brings widespread panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled panic or emotional frenzy.

clue.text: 1980s comedy film amid wrath, simply repellent

indicators.note: repellent says the hidden letters are read backwards
amid says the answer lies among the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A notoriously panned 1980s comedy is greeted with wrath as simply repellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 's comedy film amid' was misread; the definition is '1980s comedy film' and 'amid' signals the hidden run. ISHTAR (1987) starred Warren Beatty and Dustin Hoffman. 'repellent' (driving back) turns RATHSI round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar is the 1987 Hollywood comedy, famous as a box-office flop.

clue.text: Fine lord regularly invested in land

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the picked letters go into the verb

parts.note: to alight is to come down and land

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of lord

explanation.surface: A fine lord regularly puts his money into land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes L and R from lord, which go inside ALIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: All right means satisfactory or well, in the same sense as saying something is fine.

clue.text: Niche that is fun

parts.note: a nook is a recess or niche
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A secluded niche is where the fun happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Fun is a coy euphemism here: nookie is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is informal British slang for sexual activity, a playful euphemism for fun.

clue.text: Light stone's back with the concrete

indicators.note: back means the final letter of stone is taken

parts.note: concrete means actual, real rather than abstract

explanation.surface: A light stone wall is backed with concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, extremely light in weight or substance.
